summary: Inspect selected iSCSI targets in Nex Core to autofill actual LUN, native WWID and existing filesystem UUID in ordinary and clustered storage forms, with honest incomplete results, explicit multiple-LUN selection and unchanged manual exclusivity.

guide.reason: Storage steps explain selected-target detection, actual LUN zero, explicit multiple-LUN choice, transient CHAP, incomplete/unsupported identities, older-Core manual fallback and unchanged exclusivity. Troubleshooting and verification identify safe retry and native/browser limits.

api.reason: Existing POST /api/v1/storage/discover and Core storage-discover relay gain optional iSCSI target_iqn, transient iscsi_luns and storage-iscsi-inspect-v1 capability gating; Controller validates results (printable ASCII, bounded fields, at most 64 unique LUNs) and a target reporting more than 64 LUNs is refused. The backup-purpose field is gated by storage-discovery-purpose-v1. Both sides validate scope and input, keep credentials out of arguments/state/results, and preserve bounded failure/cancellation, safe observation retries and older-Core compatibility. Selected-target CHAP is limited to 255 UTF-8 bytes without narrowing target-only or SMB discovery.

roadmap.reason: Completes a local discovery workflow and records its storage-plan correction; no milestone, release or phase acceptance status changes. Existing image, clustered storage and hardware gates remain open.

state.reason: Core performs bounded read-only userspace observation using its existing initiator identity. No discovery journal, node, kernel session, mount, resource identity or durable Controller/pool record is added. Registration remains the existing Core-owned durable workflow.

verification.method: One-off, non-reproducible Core/native disposable-target smokes (throwaway runners, not retained) observed ext4/XFS/GFS2, a single GPT filesystem, blank/ambiguous media, CHAP success/refusal and empty results, with unchanged backing hashes and native/kernel records. Six concurrent observations preserved an existing session; actual context cancellation and unresponsive-peer timeout closed sockets. Focused Go suites, native C regressions, frontend types/tests/build and generated API checks passed when last run before the final review fixes; the review-fix round did not rerun the browser harnesses, full Go suites or package/image builds. independent source reviews cleared reported corrections. QA distinguishes simulated browser APIs from native target evidence and records untested deployment/image/hardware limits and the full-worktree privacy failure caused by pre-existing unrelated core dumps.
